state_of_the_evidence.claim: Silero‑VAD gate reduces the watcher’s CPU usage on the development workstation
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: DEVICE‑GENERALISATION warm‑run (5 repeats, spread < 3 %): gated watcher uses 0.23 % of a core versus ungated watcher 39.1 % of a core (ratio ≈ 170 ×). Null hypothesis: no reduction (ratio = 1).

state_of_the_evidence.claim: The previously reported 50 % banding in the empty‑room video was an artefact of an incorrect frame‑stride
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: EMPTY‑ROOM‑NULL results (corrected NV12 stride, 19 200 B/frame): empty‑room banded fraction = 0.0000 % (baseline). Null hypothesis: empty room shows 0 % banding. The earlier 50 % figure is retracted (see CAMERA‑FLICKER‑BANDING).

state_of_the_evidence.claim: A mouth‑localised visual signal survives head motion and is stronger when speaking than a cheek control
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: MOUTH‑DETECTOR results: speaking mouth region moves +0.733 sd, cheek control +0.477 sd (Δ = 0.256 sd). Null hypothesis: no difference (Δ = 0).

state_of_the_evidence.claim: A large cloud multimodal model can detect speaking from a single 160×96 greyscale frame
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: CLOUD‑MULTIMODAL results: sensitivity = 0.667 (8/12 speaking frames), false‑positive rate = 0.0 (0/12 silent frames). Null hypothesis: chance performance (0.5). Margin over null = +0.167.

state_of_the_evidence.claim: Temporal‑median row‑band removal isolates a genuine speech‑related motion signal
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: TEMPORAL‑MEDIAN‑FIX results (median across repeats): occupied flip‑rate = 0.462 ± 0.03, empty‑room flip‑rate = 0.000. Null hypothesis: no signal (flip‑rate = 0). Margin = 0.462.

state_of_the_evidence.claim: Fundamental‑frequency (F0) jumps cannot reliably identify speaker changes in this corpus
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: F0‑SPEAKER‑CHANGE results: median jump ≈ 0.3 σ, no separation between same‑speaker and different‑speaker pauses. Null hypothesis: F0 provides no discriminative power (effect = 0).

state_of_the_evidence.claim: The LLM‑director’s repeatability is limited by hosted inference nondeterminism, not by the model itself
state_of_the_evidence.evidence: LOCAL‑VLM‑VISION and DIRECTOR‑REPEATABILITY results: hosted GPT‑OSS‑120b shows 4 distinct headlines over 8 runs (spread = 0.619), deterministic stub shows 1 headline (spread = 0). Null hypothesis: deterministic behaviour (spread = 0).

unsafe_claims.claim: Silero‑VAD gate saves ~31.8 % of a CPU core (the figure quoted in commit 8eb05f6)
unsafe_claims.why: The 31.8 % figure was derived from undocumented arithmetic and does not match any reproducible measurement; the only measured numbers are 0.23 % vs 39.1 % (≈ 170 × reduction). The claim is therefore unsupported and has been retracted.
unsafe_claims.action: Remove the 31.8 % figure from all documentation and replace it with the measured ratio; do not use it for budgeting.

unsafe_claims.claim: Horizontal LED‑flicker banding is a real nuisance term that must be filtered
unsafe_claims.why: Camera‑Flicker‑Banding was withdrawn after the stride bug was fixed; the banding disappears (0 % in empty room). The claim is a false positive.
unsafe_claims.action: Delete the banding‑filter requirement from the roadmap; focus on genuine motion signals instead.

unsafe_claims.claim: The audio‑only channel is dead for speaker‑change detection
unsafe_claims.why: CLOUD‑MULTIMODAL shows a usable speech‑presence signal (sensitivity 0.667, FPR 0), contradicting the “audio dead” narrative. The claim is contradicted by measured evidence.
unsafe_claims.action: Re‑evaluate audio‑channel utility; keep the audio pipeline for speech‑presence detection.

unsafe_claims.claim: A local LLM can serve as the ‘teacher’ for the system
unsafe_claims.why: TEACHER‑PIPELINE and TEACHER‑LLM results demonstrate that the LLM teacher fails to beat its own controls and cannot be validated on the current data. The claim is falsified.
unsafe_claims.action: Discard the LLM‑teacher approach; continue using a conventional teacher once data requirements are met.

unsafe_claims.claim: Dialogue‑Intake correctly counts hand‑offs in a real recording
unsafe_claims.why: DIALOGUE‑INTAKE self‑test shows the hand‑off count is inverted (zero hand‑offs reported on a recording that contains eight). The metric does not measure the intended quantity.
unsafe_claims.action: Suspend the dialogue‑intake pipeline until the hand‑off gate is fixed or replaced.

next_experiment.title: Held‑out‑device CPU‑cost measurement of Silero‑VAD gate
next_experiment.hypothesis: On a non‑x86 embedded device the Silero‑VAD gate will still reduce the watcher’s per‑second CPU usage by at least 5 % absolute core‑time compared with an ungated watcher.
next_experiment.method: Run the same 30 s speech clip (alice01_excerpt.wav) on a representative ARM‑Cortex‑M device (e.g., Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W). Measure per‑second CPU usage (resource.getrusage) for (a) watcher with Silero‑VAD gate, (b) watcher without gate. Perform 5 independent sessions (different power‑on cycles) and report mean ± 95 % CI for each condition.
controls: Ungated watcher on the same device (baseline control).
Cold‑start flush before each 100 ms chunk to isolate cache effects (as in DEVICE‑GENERALISATION).
next_experiment.null: No reduction: gated and ungated CPU usage are equal (difference ≤ 0.5 % absolute).
next_experiment.margin_threshold: The gated condition must beat the ungated baseline by ≥ 5 % absolute core‑time (e.g., 0.05 % of a core) and the 95 % CI of the difference must not include zero.
next_experiment.falsifier: If the measured reduction is ≤ 5 % or the confidence interval includes zero, the hypothesis is rejected and the gate’s cost‑saving claim is abandoned.

debrief.biggest_risk: The held‑out‑device measurement may show that the Silero‑VAD gate provides no meaningful CPU savings on target hardware, invalidating the primary performance justification for the gate and forcing a redesign of the watcher pipeline.
debrief.what_would_change_the_plan: A clear demonstration that the gate’s CPU advantage disappears on real devices would cause us to drop the gate, remove all gate‑related budget assumptions, and pivot to alternative low‑cost VAD strategies (e.g., energy‑based hysteresis). Conversely, a strong positive result would cement the gate as a core component and shift focus to improving its detection accuracy rather than its cost.
